description:
Decided in 'How do comparable native subsets keep their rules predictable?' (defk-dtw.3), 'What is the one rule a kernel author keeps in their head?' (defk-dtw.7) and 'What does a good kernel compile error look like?' (defk-dtw.8).

- Opens with the one rule verbatim (CONTEXT.md).
- One entry per construct and type in today's subset, each marked supported / supported with restrictions / unsupported, with a short example (fenced defk + iex> lines, the format defk-rhb extracts).
- A Limits section listing every limit (i64 overflow, values that don't fit their type incl. array writes and bit segments, guard errors raising, recursion, code size).
- A divergence page generated from the Defk.Divergences registry (defk-63k); until that lands, a placeholder naming the known ones.
- An error index: one anchor per stable error code from defk-vku, with the failing example and the rewrite.
- An 'Unsupported, write this instead' table for the rejected first-write forms in 'Which convenience constructs do the six target workloads need?' (defk-dtw.18; list in the comment on defk-vku).
Feature tickets landing later add their own entries (each says so).

Done when every construct the compiler accepts today has an entry, every error code has an anchor, and the doc reads as a complete reference for a kernel author who has never seen the code.
title: Write docs/language.md: the kernel subset reference
